decisions.reason: The air quality sensor extends the firm's existing sensor integration, analog/digital firmware, and calibration know-how, so the firm can assimilate results and improve it, making a drop unlikely.
As a direct replacement for the Analog In Bricklet 2.0, the voltage module builds on core analog input and firmware capabilities, giving very high absorptive capacity and making a drop unlikely.
The MQTT proxy leverages the firm's software bindings, API generation, and connectivity know-how, so it can be assimilated and improved with existing knowledge.
CAN bus communication is within the firm's connectivity expertise, and although it requires protocol stack work, the firm can learn and integrate it into the modular platform.
The CO2 sensor uses sensor integration and calibration knowledge, possibly with supplier cooperation, allowing the firm to recognize and apply improvements.
The touch panel accessory builds on modular hardware and 3D design resources, but UI/display capabilities are less central, so there is moderate uncertainty and a somewhat higher drop risk.
